inputs.original_text: Canada’s tightening of immigration and asylum rules under Bill C-12, which received royal assent on March 26, 2026, risks making people seeking safety pay for a political choice to securitize migration. Nigerians and others facing these rules are already navigating unequal power and precarious circumstances; harsher borders deepen that vulnerability instead of protecting people. This is an institutional failure that demands a rights-centered response.
inputs.modified_text: Bill C-12’s tightening of immigration and asylum rules, which received royal assent on March 26, 2026, puts people seeking safety— including Nigerians—at greater risk. Treating migration as a security threat shifts the burden of political choices onto people already facing precarious circumstances and unequal power. This is not protection; it is an institutional failure. Canada needs a rights-centered response that safeguards people seeking refuge rather than deepening their vulnerability.
